source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Clutch and Transmissions, p.7-39

procedures.title: Turbo Hydra-Matic transmission: remove and install
steps: Install in reverse order, with one added step: before fitting the flex plate to converter bolts, check that the converter weld nuts sit flush with the flex plate and the converter turns freely by hand there.
Start all three bolts by hand and snug them finger tight before torquing to specification, to keep the converter aligned.
Take the car off the hoist and check the linkage adjustment.

procedures.title: Turbo Hydra-Matic diagnosis: sequence and checks
steps: Know which units work in each gear and shift so the fault can be narrowed to a unit or circuit.
Find out exactly what the owner is complaining about; a short ride together often helps, and may show the condition is normal and should be left alone.
Check fluid level and condition.
Check and fix the detent switch.
Check and fix the vacuum line and fittings.
Check and fix the manual linkage.
Fluid: always check before a road test; fluid must show on the dipstick before driving. Check in Park, engine running, car level.
If the level was low, look for leaks.
Manual linkage: the engine must start only in Park and Neutral; in Park the pawl must engage freely and hold the car; the quadrant pointer must line up with each range.

specs.what: fluid level at normal operating temperature (170°-190°F)

specs.value: at or slightly below ADD mark

notes: Wrong fluid level can cause erratic shifts, pump noise and other faults.
A burnt smell and discolored fluid mean burnt clutches or bands; the transmission has to come out.
The manual's text reads "warm fluid (room temperature)" for the ADD-mark reading.

procedures.title: Turbo Hydra-Matic oil leak diagnosis
steps: Find the true source first; airflow around the engine and transmission can make a leak look like it comes from elsewhere, usually carrying oil rearward (a filler tube to case leak may show at the rear of the transmission).
Wipe the area clean before looking.
Use the red dye added at the factory to tell transmission fluid from other oils; a black light comparison with the engine and transmission dipstick oil also identifies the source.
Keep the engine running while looking for the leak.
Oil pan: check bolt torque, pan gasket fit or damage, and gasket face flatness.
Rear extension: check bolt torque, rear seal, extension to case gasket, and porous casting.

Case: check filler pipe O-ring (missing, damaged, or loaded on one side by a misplaced filler pipe bracket), modulator O-ring, governor cover/gasket/bolts, speedometer gear O-ring, manual shaft seal, line pressure tap plug (stripped or short of sealer), parking pawl shaft cup plug, vent pipe (see vent pipe causes), porous case.

Front end: check front seal (also look for nicks on the converter neck, a pump bushing moved forward, or a missing garter spring on the pump to converter seal), pump bolts and seals, converter weld leak.
